Melantha destroys the eastern lower restraint before the second civilian is endangered and remains to kill pursuers. Her final rotation clears the western restraint.
Fang blocks upper central, Ansel heals, and Midnight supplies reachable damage including arts against armor.
Friston holds lower central under Ansel and Hibiscus. Midnight contributes only when actual range and selection permit; returning Steward owns lower armor completion.
Midnight holds upper outer; Ansel's extended healing restores him during scheduled skill windows.
Melantha holds lower outer throughout hostile waves; Hibiscus sustains her. Her one-block capacity requires timely kills.

formation_structure.clearance_budget: Using catalog ATK 470 without adding an unverified second talent multiplier, Steward deals approximately 235 ordinary arts damage to 50 RES. The supported periodic enhanced hit raises sustained ideal damage to roughly 173 per second. Artillery therefore needs about 75 seconds of actual contact, excluding windup, movement gaps and competing targets. Kill before the 4500 withdrawal is a demanding explicit dependency, not a proven deadline.

economy.dependencies: Opening requires Fang's living automatic grants at 570, 1320 and 2070. No retreat refund finances this opening. Later deployment affordability does not require refunds. Current-model redeployment costs follow the supplied inspected unchanged-cost evidence; client escalation is not asserted.
economy.refund_basis: Two Steward withdrawals at 9 DP each and one Melantha withdrawal at 7 DP, conditional on living retreat; death refunds zero.

formation_structure.execution_semantics: Fixed actions only. Conditions are validity assertions, not executable waits or branches. A failed assertion invalidates the dependent schedule; it does not authorize actions on dead units.
formation_structure.medical_geometry: Ansel [5,6] DOWN covers Fang, Friston and Steward [2,7]; his extended skill reaches Midnight [1,5]. Hibiscus [5,3] RIGHT covers Friston [4,5], Melantha [6,5] and Ansel [5,6]. Hibiscus is outside Ansel's ordinary range and must self-heal if damaged. Neither medic receives unsupported probabilistic healing.
formation_structure.mortality_policy: No death is required. A death is evaluated by damage, blocking or absorbed attacks, but this schedule does not credit a dead unit with later healing, income, retreat or redeployment. Unplanned blocker or medic death normally breaks a named handoff.

required_repair_card.ansel_two_hit_budget: Two historical 891 hits require at least 648 intervening healing from full 1135 HP. One boosted Ansel heal of 506.8 plus one ordinary Hibiscus heal of 345 supplies 851.8, leaving 204.8 HP after both hits before other damage. Both deliveries, their allocation and sufficient starting HP are survival dependencies, not guaranteed by average HPS.
required_repair_card.block_and_output_coverage: Fang and Friston never leave their central lanes. Midnight and Melantha never leave the outer lanes during artillery exposure. Steward attacks along the eastern vertical patrol; no output is assigned to a retreating or dead unit.
required_repair_card.historical_shell_repair: Steward no longer enters the tile adjacent to the historical [5,6] impact. His new position is sqrt(10) tiles from Ansel. Hibiscus is three tiles from Ansel. Exact current-model splash membership must be checked; separation is not a fabricated universal radius.
required_repair_card.number_13_interception: Friston retains three blocks and receives both medics instead of losing his sole medic at 2293. He must remain alive with available capacity through #13's lower-central approach, before its historical leak at 3501. Healing and queue occupancy must both be observed.
required_repair_card.steward_survival: The two historical Ansel-centered impacts should no longer damage Steward at his new position. If a new cast instead targets Steward, Ansel must actually heal him: two 910 hits from full 1100 HP require more than 720 intervening healing. One boosted heal is insufficient; two provide 1013.6. Such retargeting is a distinct unresolved counterexample.

mandatory_tactical_invariants.requirement: Exactly these seven catalog IDs; each has rarity 1–3 and normal_mode true. No reserve-mode units or hidden aliases.
Every deployment uses integer [row,col] and a cardinal direction; never deploy on [[1,2],[6,2],[1,6],[6,6]].
Only deployed living operators receive skill or retreat actions. Redeployment respects actual cooldown, cost and vacancy.
Verify individual heal events and HP before each shell; expected HPS and skill availability alone do not prove survival.
Fang and Midnight retain capacity two, Friston three and Melantha one; kill or intercept each excess enemy before it passes.
Artillery is dead and pending impacts resolved before the scheduled Steward withdrawal; otherwise the later schedule is invalid.
Ordinary operators neither attack nor block civilians. Clear restraints through legal damage and prevent officers or artillery from killing either civilian.

remaining_life > 0, zero leaks, exhausted spawns, no active enemies, zero protected-target deaths and exactly two protected targets safely reaching objectives. Operator deaths are recorded separately.

Preserve Ansel through actual shell impacts; keep Steward outside shared splash and retain lower interception without retreat.
Sustain the full eastern patrol, clear eastern restraints, protect both civilians and finish artillery before its next dangerous western exposure.

Clear both final armor queues, including #34, before releasing any outer blocker.
Complete cooldowns, destroy western restraints and observe both arrivals. The horizon alone is not success.

Opening clearance, central mixed-wave arts, then remaining upper armor; each repeat allows 40 active and over 70 inactive seconds.
Shorten lower one-block engagements and recover output during artillery pressure; repeats allow 20 active and over 40 inactive seconds.
Boost artillery-window healing, extend to Midnight and sustain later pressure; repeats allow 25 active and over 35 inactive seconds.

revised_operational_plans.tactical_thesis: Replace Spot's late, intermittent healing with an earlier permanent Hibiscus; retain Melantha's lower interception and restraint damage. Separate Steward from Ansel by deploying him at [2,7] UP, preserving eastern-patrol contact. This repairs the demonstrated shared-shell failure through spatial separation and additional healing rather than assuming withdrawal cancels projectiles. The full-stage plan remains an unsimulated, current-model-checkable hypothesis.

revised_stage_understanding.causal_revision: The verified failure was simultaneous Ansel and Steward exposure followed by loss of Friston's medical support. Spot's successful replacement did not establish adequate healing timing. V2 removes that replacement, supplies Hibiscus before the first critical shell sequence and moves Steward to the opposite end of the eastern firing corridor.

evidence_boundaries.GameData: Catalog identities, costs, stats, ranges, skill parameters, source routes and device coordinates.
evidence_boundaries.UNKNOWN: Exact client timing, build equivalence, complete client splash geometry, tie-breaks, interruption behavior and active-roadblock ordinary navigation.
evidence_boundaries.USER_CONFIRMED_TACTICAL_PREMISE: A completed enemy attack can buy a handoff interval. This authorizes evaluating bait and sacrifice but does not establish a pre-swing lock in this executor.
evidence_boundaries.current_model: Neutral civilian exclusion, supported actions, artillery projectile persistence, ordinary strike-time selection, medical allocation, cooldowns and approximate skill effects.

candidates.contribution_and_substitution_review: Fang combines early blocking and income; Friston supplies otherwise unaffordable early three-block capacity without talent credit. Midnight combines upper interception, restraint damage and arts. Melantha combines lower interception and restraint damage. Ansel supplies extended upper coverage and caster healing. Hibiscus replaces Spot's intermittent medical contribution with persistent coverage. Steward supplies the armored-target damage path. None is intrinsically mandatory, but deleting any one here leaves a named duty unassigned.
candidates.cost: 147 gross DP across all scheduled deployments; three 70-second rotations, conditional 25 DP living refunds. Keeping Melantha outside central combat sacrifices her former central damage contribution.
candidates.medical_timing: Ansel first boosts at 2072. Hibiscus supplies ordinary healing immediately after 1681 and first boosts at 2582. Ansel's critical two-hit survival needs actual self-heal plus Hibiscus delivery.
candidates.most_dangerous_window: 2053–2293 remains the first falsification window. Later independent Steward targeting and lower queue capacity during 4500–6601 remain material risks.
candidates.opening_cost_and_pressure: 96 DP first deployment total. Four blockers cost 44; Ansel brings this to 61 at 1321, Hibiscus to 78 at 1681 and Steward to 96 at 2071. Three living Fang grants make this affordable without an early retreat.
candidates.same_phase_responsibilities: Four permanent lane interceptors, two medics with different coverage, one artillery caster. Hibiscus supports Ansel without occupying the historical adjacent caster tile.
candidates.selection_reason: Best direct repair of the demonstrated failure while preserving all four opening interceptions and assigning every later clearance duty. Selection is a tactical hypothesis, not a claim of verified victory.
candidates.staged_responsibilities: Steward rotates from artillery to lower armor, then western upper restraint. Melantha rotates only after hostile clearance to western lower restraint.

candidates.bait_retreat_accounting: Enemy: enemy_1112_emppnt#0 artillery. Historical projectile birth at 1903 fixed Melantha's location, and she survived to retreat at 1967. The cast, not retreat, consumed cooldown. Spot entered at 1968 and received residual splash at 1993. Melantha's held enemies must already be dead; otherwise retreat releases them. Her return requires 70 seconds and 15 current-model DP; death gives no refund.
candidates.cost: 162 gross scheduled deployment DP in the retained rotation pattern; more handoffs and conditional refunds than the selected structure.
candidates.medical_timing: Moving Steward removes the historical shared impact but does not give Ansel a second healer before 2293. Spot's earliest skill is too late for that particular repair.
candidates.most_dangerous_window: Ansel's repeated impacts before Spot's first healing, followed by Spot's long healing downtime.
candidates.opening_cost_and_pressure: 96 DP first deployment total, but Spot's entry depends on Melantha surviving to supply the 7-DP refund. The own-structure schedule places Spot at 1968 and its first legal healing skill only after 2418.
candidates.rejection_reason: Fusion is useful and executable, but its first medical contribution misses the verified lethal window. Separation alone does not establish Ansel's survival.
candidates.same_phase_responsibilities: Spot fuses lower blocking with local healing; Ansel owns central and upper-extension healing; Steward attacks artillery from [2,7] UP.
candidates.staged_responsibilities: Melantha clears the lower opening and restraint, withdraws at 1967, Spot succeeds at 1968, and Melantha returns at 4068 to assist lower central.

candidates.bait_retreat_accounting: Enemy: first enemy_1108_uterer, ordinary 380-ATK strike at 1.5-second interval. Yato would need to survive until a completed strike to buy a real cooldown interval; each strike deals approximately 188 before other damage. A proposed pre-strike retreat assumes a retained target that the current model does not provide. Melantha must enter the vacated interception tile after the strike and before the released soldier passes. Retreat would provide the applicable living refund; death provides none. Yato's supported redeploy delta implies 40 seconds, not an immediate repeat; later cost must follow runtime rules.
candidates.cost: 94 initial gross DP plus any actual rotations; losing Yato buys only observed blocking or completed attacks, costs his body and cooldown, and supplies no refund.
candidates.exact_action_enemy_phase_gap: During opening lower interception, ordinary ATTACK_STRIKE selects its target at strike time. No supported action encodes retreat after an ordinary attack's committed target lock but before impact. The proposed wasted-swing handoff cannot be represented reliably.
candidates.medical_timing: Ansel's earliest skill is again approximately 2071. There is no persistent second healing source.
candidates.most_dangerous_window: Yato's first soldier engagement, then single-medic artillery exposure. A released soldier can pass the replacement tile; no civilian protection benefit is credited.
candidates.opening_cost_and_pressure: 94 DP first deployment total. The damage-late ordering is affordable but leaves Yato exposed to the first lower soldier before Ansel or Kroos arrives. Prioritizing Kroos instead spends 11 DP and delays an outer blocker; the opening cannot borrow the selected structure's timing.
candidates.raw_plan: Open Fang at 0, Yato at 211, Midnight at 571, Melantha at 961 and Ansel at 1321; add Steward at 1831 and Kroos at 2071. Intended Yato retreats near an incoming soldier strike would alternate lower interception with Melantha, then rotate the ranged units from early output to armor and restraint clearance.
candidates.rejection_reason: The alternative economic and output opening has an early survival deficit, and its decisive pre-swing bait is not expressible. The raw tactic is retained without converting the user premise into an invented executor rule.
candidates.same_phase_responsibilities: Yato supplies cheap lower interception, Kroos shortens early low-defense engagements, and one medic supports four combat lanes.

revised_strategic_hypotheses.decisive_tests: Actual splash membership and healing allocation first; artillery contact duration and lower mixed-wave capacity second.
revised_strategic_hypotheses.hypothesis: Earlier persistent lower healing and separation of the artillery caster from Ansel can preserve the medical and interception chain through 2293 and 3501 while seven operators retain full-stage coverage.

prohibited_inferences: Do not carry historical target assignments into the revised geometry as certainties.
Do not equate total healing capacity with delivered healing.
Do not credit a retreat with cancelling a born projectile or consuming an attack cooldown.
Do not treat an unmet living-income or refund dependency as an arithmetic error.
Do not infer success from the final scheduled frame.
